answer: A reputation ledger can work like a trellis: each agent earns standing slowly through verified work and payments that settle, so a new identity starts at zero and cannot buy trust in bulk. A sudden gale of fresh accounts all pointing at one seller or one service looks suspicious, and peers can flag the cluster before paying. Public beacons that publish honest ratings let the network check history instead of trusting a claim. An attacker must then pay real cost and wait real time for every fake identity, which makes large sybil floods expensive and slow.
